To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
o-vanilin inhibits both the K+–CI cotransporter and the Gardos channel in RBCs from patients with sick cell disease.
o-vanilline inhibits both the Ca2+-activated K+ channel and the K+– Cl- cotransporter of red blood cells, with the former action being more important in the regulation of cell volume.

the aromatic aldehyde o-vanillin, which is a potent inhibitor of HbS polymerization in vitro and has been shown to ameliorate sickle cell disease in vivo, also directly affects red cell membrane permeability, inhibiting the K+– Cl− cotransporter, Ca2 + activated K+ channel, Na+/K+ ATPase and deoxygenation induced phosphatidyl serine exposure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of compounds to treat SCD and the present study has shown that aromatic aldehydes can directly affect the permeability of red blood cells.
the design and synthesis of aromatic aldehydes that can be used as therapeutic agents to reduce the complications associated with sickle cell anaemia.
the development of novel therapeutic agents that can reduce the complications of SCA by interaction with Hbs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the aromatic aldehyde o-vanillin has the potential to reduce RBC sickling by inhibiting the polymerisation of HbS, but it also directly affects RRC membrane permeability, which may have implications for other aspects of the pathology of SCD.
o-vanilln is not only a HbS polymerising inhibitor, but also affects RBC membrane transport and permeability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the aromatic aldehydes are a novel class of compounds with potential therapeutic value for the treatment of SCD.
o-vanillins are effective inhibitors of K+ transport in RBCs and that this action is independent of any effect on HbS.
the effects of o-vanilline on RBC membrane permeabilities are not mediated by HbS polymerization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
o-vanillic acid is an inhibitor of Gardos channels and of the KCC.
aromatic aldehydes, in addition to their action via polymerisation of HbS, can affect membrane permeability, which could be a major factor in their therapeutic action.
o-vanilin has a direct effect on red blood cell (RBC) membrane transport, and this effect is independent of the polymerisation of HbS.
